message: In the twin under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit concept, the crowd comfort verification has peak acceleration uncertainty, thank you Vibration Control Specialist and thank you Structural Dynamics Lead. To check it I used the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6) against the comfort target assumption (C1). I found reduction from 17.50 metres per second squared to 0.74 metres per second squared with 9.44 percent effective damping and 20.0 millimetres travel, reaching Comfort Level (CL) CL2 below 1.0 metre per second squared, according to Setra, 2006. I propose accepting CL2 as comfortable retrofit level for the lively baseline. My position: ready because damping increase and acceleration reduction are demonstrated. In the concealed mounting concept, the install and maintenance access has closure and visibility risk, thank you Retrofit Integration Architect. To check it I used the concealed mounting detail sketch (E9) with the Den Hartog optimum result (E3) and the phased install plan (C4). I found zero hardware above deck with paired 250 kilogram units tuned to 1.81 hertz installable from below with no deck closure, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose night-time clamp-beam install and six-monthly soffit-hatch inspection with annual re-tuning. My position: ready because invisible and maintainable build is shown.
